events.text: Lunar New Year: the whole house folds dumplings, and one of them hides a coin for luck.

choices.text: Eat until you find the coin

effects.log: Forty dumplings later, you find it. Luck for the year, and a stomach ache.
Yours are ugly and taste the best.

events.text: New Year: the elders hand out red envelopes to the young, and to anyone who bows deeply enough.

effects.log: A pocket full of red envelopes. (12 taels)

choices.text: Give red envelopes to the children

effects.log: Twenty children chasing you through the street. (−10 taels)

events.text: Firecrackers at midnight to drive away the Nian beast. The whole town sounds like a battlefield.

effects.log: Your ears ring for three days. No beasts were seen.
The whole town glows red. It is the most beautiful noise in the world.

events.text: The Lantern Festival: riddles hang from every lantern, and a correct answer wins a sweet.

ok.log: Eleven riddles, eleven sweets. The riddle-writer asks your name.

fail.log: You win one sweet, for a riddle a child had already solved.

effects.log: A river of light. Somewhere in it, someone smiles at you.

events.text: Sweet rice balls in syrup for the Lantern Festival, and a whole neighbourhood eating together in the street.

effects.log: Sticky fingers, loud stories, full bellies.

choices.text: Carry bowls to the old widows

effects.log: Every widow on the street gets a bowl, and tells you her life story.

events.text: Qingming: families sweep the graves of their ancestors and burn paper money for the afterlife.

effects.log: You pull the weeds and tell the ancestors about your year. It feels like they listen.
A grave nobody visits. You sweep it and leave a flower.

events.text: The Qingming kite-flying: whole families on the hills, kites shaped like dragons, swallows and centipedes.

effects.log: It flies higher than the temple. You feel like a child again.

choices.text: Cut the string and let it go

effects.log: An old custom: let the bad luck fly away with the kite.

events.text: The Dragon Boat Festival: drums, paddles and a whole river screaming.

ok.log: Your boat wins by a dragon's nose. You are carried home.

fail.log: Your boat comes third. The zongzi afterwards are still excellent.

effects.log: Sticky rice in bamboo leaves, and the best view of the race.

events.text: On Dragon Boat day, parents paint the character for 'king' on their children's foreheads with realgar paste to ward off evil.

choices.text: Let an old woman paint yours

effects.log: You walk around all day with "king" on your forehead. It suits you.
The house smells sharp and green. No evil comes, as far as you can tell.

events.text: Qixi: the night the Weaver Girl and the Herdsman meet across the Milky Way. Young people make wishes on the stars.

effects.log: You wish for someone. Somewhere, possibly, someone wishes back.

choices.text: Tell the old story to the children

effects.log: Magpies, a bridge of wings, one night a year. The children sigh.

events.text: Qixi custom: girls float needles on a bowl of water. If the needle's shadow looks like a flower, she will be clever.

effects.log: Your shadow looks like a sword. Everyone decides that counts.
You declare every shadow a flower. You are very popular.

events.text: Mid-Autumn: the fullest moon of the year, mooncakes, and families together under the sky.

effects.log: Lotus paste, salted egg yolk, and everyone you love within arm's reach.

choices.text: Write a poem to the moon

effects.log: The moon does not answer. The poem is still good.

events.text: Mid-Autumn far from home. Everyone else in the inn is also far from home, looking at the same moon.

effects.log: By midnight the inn is a family. Strangers become friends under the moon.

choices.text: Look at the moon and think of home

effects.log: Somewhere, someone at home is looking at the same moon. You are sure of it.

events.text: The harvest festival: songpyeon rice cakes steamed on pine needles, and the whole village dancing in a circle under the moon.

effects.log: Round and round until you are dizzy and happy.
Pine-needle smell in your hair for a week.

events.text: Double Ninth: people climb mountains, drink chrysanthemum tea and remember the old.

effects.log: Slow, steady, and full of stories. At the top, the whole valley.
She protests the whole way and tells everyone at the top that you are her favourite.

events.text: Double Ninth is the festival of the old. The village holds a feast for everyone over seventy.

effects.log: You pour tea for sixty old people. Every one of them has advice.
Stories of wars, floods and loves nobody else remembers.

events.text: Winter Solstice: red bean porridge to keep away the cold and the spirits, and the longest night of the year.

effects.log: Warm to your toes. No spirits dare.
You meditate through the longest night. At dawn your breath is like the returning sun.

events.text: In the north they say that if you do not eat dumplings at the solstice, your ears will freeze off.

effects.log: Your ears survive the winter.
Your ears survive. You are still slightly worried.
